+"""Export a machine-readable description of a prompt.
+
+This module deliberately depends only on the standard library so that
+documentation tooling can import it without pulling in Click's prompt or
+terminal handling code.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import typing as t
+
+__all__ = ["build_prompt_schema"]
+
+
+def build_prompt_schema(
+    text: str,
+    suffix: str,
+    show_default: bool = False,
+    default: t.Any | None = None,
+    show_choices: bool = True,
+    type: t.Any | None = None,
+) -> dict[str, t.Any]:
+    """Describe a prompt as a JSON-serializable dict.
+
+    Unlike an interactive prompt renderer, nothing is interpolated into the
+    text and no input is read. The result has four fields:
+
+    ``text``
+        The prompt text, unmodified.
+    ``suffix``
+        The prompt suffix, unmodified.
+    ``default``
+        The raw ``default`` value if ``show_default`` is true, otherwise
+        ``None``. The caller is responsible for passing a JSON-compatible
+        value.
+    ``choices``
+        ``str()`` of each item in ``type.choices`` if ``show_choices`` is
+        true and the type has choices, otherwise an empty list. A missing
+        ``type`` or ``choices`` attribute is not an error.
+
+    :param text: The prompt text.
+    :param suffix: The suffix shown after the prompt.
+    :param show_default: Whether to include the default value.
+    :param default: The default value. Must be JSON-compatible.
+    :param show_choices: Whether to include the type's choices.
+    :param type: An object that may have a ``choices`` attribute, such as a
+        ``click.Choice`` instance.
+    """
+    choices: list[str] = []
+
+    if show_choices and type is not None:
+        type_choices = getattr(type, "choices", None)
+
+        if type_choices:
+            choices = [str(choice) for choice in type_choices]
+
+    return {
+        "text": text,
+        "suffix": suffix,
+        "default": default if show_default else None,
+        "choices": choices,
+    }

+++ b/tests/test_standalone_prompt_schema.py
@@ -0,0 +1,118 @@
+import enum
+import importlib.util
+import json
+import pathlib
+import subprocess
+import sys
+
+import pytest
+
+import click
+from click.termui import _build_prompt
+
+MODULE_PATH = (
+    pathlib.Path(__file__).parent.parent / "src" / "standalone_prompt_schema.py"
+)
+
+
+def _load_module():
+    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
+        "standalone_prompt_schema", MODULE_PATH
+    )
+    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
+    return module
+
+
+build_prompt_schema = _load_module().build_prompt_schema
+
+
+class Color(enum.Enum):
+    RED = "red"
+    BLUE = "blue"
+
+
+def test_text_and_suffix_are_separate_and_unmodified():
+    result = build_prompt_schema("Name", ": ")
+    assert result == {"text": "Name", "suffix": ": ", "default": None, "choices": []}
+    assert _build_prompt("Name", ": ") == "Name: "
+
+
+def test_default_shown_is_raw_not_bracketed():
+    choice = click.Choice(["a", "b"])
+    result = build_prompt_schema("Pick", ": ", True, "a", True, choice)
+    assert result == {
+        "text": "Pick",
+        "suffix": ": ",
+        "default": "a",
+        "choices": ["a", "b"],
+    }
+    assert _build_prompt("Pick", ": ", True, "a", True, choice) == "Pick (a, b) [a]: "
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("default", [0, 1.5, False, [1, 2], {"k": "v"}, "x"])
+def test_default_raw_value_preserved(default):
+    result = build_prompt_schema("Q", "? ", show_default=True, default=default)
+    assert result["default"] == default
+    assert type(result["default"]) is type(default)
+    assert result["text"] == "Q"
+
+
+def test_default_hidden_when_show_default_false():
+    result = build_prompt_schema("Q", ": ", show_default=False, default="x")
+    assert result["default"] is None
+
+
+def test_choices_hidden_when_show_choices_false():
+    choice = click.Choice(["a", "b"])
+    result = build_prompt_schema("Q", ": ", show_choices=False, type=choice)
+    assert result["choices"] == []
+
+
+def test_choices_are_stringified():
+    choice = click.Choice([1, 2, Color.RED])
+    result = build_prompt_schema("Q", ": ", type=choice)
+    assert result["choices"] == ["1", "2", str(Color.RED)]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("type", [None, click.INT, object(), click.Choice([])])
+def test_missing_choices_is_not_an_error(type):
+    assert build_prompt_schema("Q", ": ", type=type)["choices"] == []
+
+
+def test_duck_typed_choices():
+    class Fake:
+        choices = ("x", "y")
+
+    assert build_prompt_schema("Q", ": ", type=Fake())["choices"] == ["x", "y"]
+    # The original only renders choices for click.Choice instances.
+    assert _build_prompt("Q", ": ", type=Fake()) == "Q: "
+
+
+def test_result_is_json_serializable():
+    choice = click.Choice([1, Color.BLUE])
+    result = build_prompt_schema("Q", ": ", True, {"a": [1]}, True, choice)
+    assert json.loads(json.dumps(result)) == result
+
+
+def test_reads_no_input(monkeypatch):
+    def fail(*args, **kwargs):
+        raise AssertionError("input must not be read")
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr("builtins.input", fail)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(sys, "stdin", None)
+    build_prompt_schema("Q", ": ", True, "d")
+
+
+def test_importable_without_click():
+    code = (
+        "import sys, importlib.util\n"
+        "sys.modules['click'] = None\n"
+        f"spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('m', {str(MODULE_PATH)!r})\n"
+        "m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)\n"
+        "spec.loader.exec_module(m)\n"
+        "loaded = [k for k, v in sys.modules.items() if v and k.startswith('click')]\n"
+        "assert not loaded, loaded\n"
+        "print(m.build_prompt_schema('a', 'b'))\n"
+    )
+    subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", code], check=True)
notes:
Added a standard-library-only build_prompt_schema that returns {text, suffix, default, choices} without building a prompt string: default is included only when show_default is true, choices are read from type.choices by attribute lookup. Tests load the module by file path, compare it against _build_prompt on the same inputs, and check JSON round-tripping, that no input is read, and that the module imports with click blocked.
